records.text: Chewy identifies several supplier-related risks. A significant portion of its private brand and non-consumable suppliers are located in China, and political/economic instability, financial instability of suppliers, labor problems, currency fluctuations, tariffs, trade restrictions, and natural disasters could disrupt its outsourcing partners and adversely affect its business [4]. The company also relies on suppliers with limited supply capabilities and has experienced disruptions where suppliers were unable to timely or cost-effectively provide products, which could impair growth if it continues [9]. There is a risk that significant suppliers could discontinue selling to Chewy or discontinue preferential pricing/exclusive incentives, and because pet food buyers are reluctant to switch products, losing a key supplier could be especially harmful [9]. Chewy also faces competitive risk if it cannot identify new suppliers or replace lost ones, and if premium pet food brands become more widely available through supermarkets, warehouse clubs, or mass merchants, or if such retailers offer these brands at lower prices, Chewy's sales and margins could suffer [8]. Additionally, a reduction or discontinuance of trade allowances, cooperative advertising, and market development fund incentives from suppliers—or competitors receiving better incentives—could reduce profitability or competitive advantage [8]. Finally, Chewy is dependent on suppliers to comply with product safety laws, and failures by suppliers (including private brand manufacturers) to meet safety or quality standards could lead to recalls, litigation, or loss of consumer confidence [7].

The company also notes that laws in certain countries may not protect or allow enforcement of intellectual property rights to the same extent as U.S. laws, exposing Nike to significant expenses and liability, and potential adverse effects on business or financial condition if it cannot successfully protect its rights or resolve conflicts [8]. Finally, Nike highlights emerging risks from developing regulations around new technologies like generative AI, which may give rise to intellectual property infringement claims or reputational harm [8][9].
